details: Bitcoin's price slid over 2% to around $77,363 on September 1st, reversing recent gains. This downturn is attributed to escalating US-Iran geopolitical tensions and associated oil price spikes, coupled with rising expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike. The combination has fostered a "risk-off" sentiment in financial markets, potentially reducing liquidity for cryptocurrencies.
title: Bitcoin Dips as US-Iran Tensions Escalate, Fed Hike Odds Rise

details: Ethereum (ETH) is currently trading near $2,452, with analysts indicating that maintaining the $2,438 weekly support level is crucial for a bullish September outlook, potentially targeting $2,920. Factors such as continued inflows into spot ETFs, growing institutional accumulation, and the development of staking products are seen as key drivers. However, repeated rejections around the $2,550 mark suggest that consolidation and volatility may precede a stronger rally.
title: Ethereum Eyes Bullish September, Holding Above Key $2,438 Support

details: Goldman Sachs, alongside 21 other major global financial institutions including Bank of America and Citigroup, plans to form a joint company this year. Their objective is to issue a U.S. dollar-pegged stablecoin by the first half of 2027, marking a significant entry of traditional finance into the stablecoin market. This initiative aims to facilitate payments and digital asset trading, adhering to regulations like the US GENIUS Act and EU MiCA.
title: Goldman Sachs, 21 Banks Partner for Dollar-Backed Stablecoin

details: The UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) is set to open its crypto authorization gateway on September 30, 2026. This new five-month window will allow crypto firms to apply for full operating licenses, transitioning the UK from a registration-only model to one with authorization standards comparable to traditional financial services. The new regulatory regime will come into effect on October 25, 2027.
title: FCA Opens Crypto Licensing Gateway in UK This Month

details: US-listed spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) witnessed substantial inflows of approximately $3.5 billion during August 2026. This marks the largest monthly intake since July 2025, with BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) alone accounting for about 88% of these net inflows. This trend signals a renewed and robust institutional demand for Bitcoin.
title: US Spot Bitcoin ETFs Log $3.5 Billion Inflows in August

details: Several decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols have recently suffered significant security breaches. Cronos validators implemented a transaction history erase to contain a $75 million lending protocol exploit. Separately, Ontology temporarily halted its mainnet due to a potential security issue. Additionally, protocols Tectonic and Moonwell were collectively targeted in attacks resulting in $83 million in losses through price manipulation tactics.
title: DeFi Protocols Hit by $75M+ Exploits on Cronos, Ontology, Tectonic, Moonwell
